workflow.title: Software RAID workflow
workflow.step_prepare: Prepare RAID member partitions on physical disks.
workflow.step_create: Create an MD array from those member partitions.
workflow.step_use: Use the MD array as a storage volume later.

create_md.title: Create MD array (software)
create_md.member_selection_help: Select existing RAID member partitions, for example /dev/sdb1. Do not select raw physical disks such as /dev/sdb.
create_md.no_eligible_members: No eligible RAID member partitions detected. Prepare Linux RAID Autodetect partitions on ESOS first.

cluster_execution.title: Multi-node cluster MD creation
cluster_execution.description: This SAN belongs to a cluster. The MD array will be created directly on each node with the validated mappings; Sync config is not used to create MD superblocks on peers.

mapping.reused_description: {count} partition mapping(s) were derived from the previous RAID preparation.
mapping.title: Resolve partition mapping
mapping.description: /dev/sdX names are not reliable across nodes. Explicitly choose which peer-node partition corresponds to each source partition before continuing.
mapping.duplicate_target: This peer partition is already selected for another source partition.
mapping.incomplete: Select a peer partition for every ambiguous mapping.
mapping.ready: Mappings are complete. Re-run cluster preflight.

form.step_description: Set the /dev/mdX name, RAID level, and chunk size before preflight. The MD array can later be used as a storage volume.
form.array_name_help: Example md0, md1. The name md0 creates the MD array /dev/md0.
form.array_name_invalid: The name must start with md and end with a number, for example md0.
form.raid_level_help: Choose the level based on redundancy and the number of available partitions.
form.level_10: RAID 10 — Stripe of mirrors, minimum 4 partitions
form.chunk_help: 64 KiB matches the ESOS examples and is a good default.
form.min_devices_error: RAID {level} requires at least {min} partitions. Selected: {count}.
form.raid10_even_error: RAID 10 requires an even number of partitions.

create_md.done_description: Array {path} was created. Software arrays and block devices have been refreshed.
create_md.next_step_lvm: Create an LVM stack (PV/VG/LV) on this array if your deployment uses LVM.
create_md.next_step_scst: Create a filesystem or SCST target / mapping according to your storage workflow.
create_md.resync_notice: Resync in progress — the array is active and listed as resync.
create_md.persisted_notice: mdadm configuration saved on the node.
create_md.persisted_partial: mdadm configuration saved on some nodes only.

prepare_partitions.title: Prepare RAID member partitions
prepare_partitions.destructive_description: This preparation replaces the partition table on the selected physical disks. It creates one RAID member partition per disk and does not run mdadm --create.
prepare_partitions.physical_disk_selection_help: Select whole physical disks, for example /dev/sdb. One RAID member partition, for example /dev/sdb1, will be created on each selected disk.
prepare_partitions.no_eligible_physical_disks: No eligible whole physical disks detected.
prepare_partitions.allow_overwrite_label: Allow overwriting existing signatures and partition tables on the selected physical disks.
prepare_partitions.done_description: Block devices have been refreshed. You can now create an MD array from these RAID member partitions.

cluster_execution.title: Multi-node cluster RAID write
cluster_execution.description: This SAN belongs to a cluster. Partitions will be prepared directly on each node with the validated mapping; Sync config is not used for this destructive operation.
cluster_execution.partitions_visible: RAID member partitions should now be visible on each cluster node.

mapping.title: Resolve disk mapping
mapping.description: /dev/sdX names are not reliable across nodes. Explicitly choose which peer-node disk corresponds to each source disk before any destructive operation.
mapping.duplicate_target: This peer disk is already selected for another source disk.
mapping.incomplete: Select a peer disk for every ambiguous mapping.
mapping.ready: Mappings are complete. Re-run cluster preflight.

partition_table.label: Physical disk partition scheme
partition_table.gpt_description: Recommended for modern systems. Creates a GPT table and enables the RAID flag.
partition_table.dos_description: Matches legacy ESOS documentation: Linux RAID type fd partition.
partition_table.auto_description: Chooses GPT when parted is available, otherwise MBR/DOS with sfdisk.

preflight.partition_table_replaced: The partition table will be replaced.

cluster_card.description: Global HA configuration for the cluster. Storage remains attached to the primary node.
cluster_card.no_primary_storage: No primary node detected for this cluster

ldap_tls_verify_disabled.title: TLS verification disabled
ldap_tls_verify_disabled.description: Without certificate verification, a man-in-the-middle attack can intercept LDAP/LDAPS traffic. Laboratory use only.

ldap_plain_no_starttls_remote.title: Plain LDAP without StartTLS
ldap_plain_no_starttls_remote.description: In production, the server rejects remote ldap:// without StartTLS. Use ldaps:// or ldap:// with StartTLS.

ldap_localhost_plain.title: LDAP to localhost
ldap_localhost_plain.description: Unencrypted connection allowed for local development only. In production prefer LDAPS or StartTLS.

oidc_issuer_no_https.title: Issuer without HTTPS
oidc_issuer_no_https.description: OIDC issuers use HTTPS in practice. Production SSO redirects require HTTPS on the application side (secure cookies).

mfa_idp_required.title: MFA required at IdP
mfa_idp_required.description: The ID token must contain recognized MFA indicators (amr or acr claims per server logic). Check your provider configuration.

mfa_idp_preferred.title: MFA “preferred”
mfa_idp_preferred.description: This mode does not block sign-in if the token lacks MFA indicators; it is informational (similar to off for rejection).

mapping_no_rules.title: No mapping rules
mapping_no_rules.description: Without rules, new JIT accounts keep the default role below. Existing accounts are not blocked.

jit_default_admin.title: Default administrator role (JIT)
jit_default_admin.description: Granting admin by default to every new external account is dangerous in production. Prefer viewer or operator with explicit rules.

page.title: Authentication providers
page.subtitle: Configure SSO (OIDC) and directory (LDAP). Changes apply after save. Secrets are never returned in clear text by the API.

oidc.cardSubtitle: SSO sign-in, token validation, and MFA policy on the ID token.
oidc.enableHelp: Shows the SSO sign-in button on the sign-in page.
oidc.issuerDesc: HTTPS provider URL without secret. Used for OpenID discovery (/.well-known/openid-configuration).
oidc.clientIdDesc: Public application identifier registered with the IdP.
oidc.clientSecretDesc: Enter only to set or replace the secret. Never shown after save; leave empty to keep the current server-side value.
oidc.secretStateDesc: Shows whether a secret is already stored. The API never returns the value.
oidc.scopesDesc: Space-separated. The openid scope is required to obtain an ID token.
oidc.redirectPathDesc: Internal HTTP path; the full URL must be registered with the IdP. The real URL may differ behind a reverse proxy (see preview).
oidc.callbackPreviewDesc: Built from the current browser origin + the path above. In production, secure cookies require HTTPS.
oidc.clockSkewDesc: Allowed margin for OIDC token validation when client/server/IdP clocks differ slightly.
oidc.mfaPolicyLabel: MFA policy on the ID token
oidc.mfaPolicyDesc: Required = OIDC sign-in denied if the token lacks recognized MFA indicators. Off / preferred = no denial on this basis (preferred does not enforce MFA).
oidc.httpsProdDesc: OIDC redirects and secure session cookies require HTTPS when NODE_ENV=production and secure cookies are enabled.
oidc.mfaRecommendDesc: In production, requiring MFA at the IdP (Required mode) helps limit session takeover; other modes do not block sign-in without MFA indicators.
oidc.pkceBody: PKCE (S256), state and nonce parameters to limit interception and replay.
oidc.correlationBody: preferred_username, else local-part of email, else sub (not configurable here).
oidc.mappingRolesBody: Fine-grained group/claim to ESOS role mapping is done via JSON rules (dedicated section).
oidc.testDesc: Checks that issuer and client_id can fetch OpenID metadata (no secrets displayed).

ldap.cardSubtitle: Directory, TLS, and service account for user lookup.
ldap.enableHelp: Shows the directory sign-in form on the sign-in page.
ldap.modeSummaryDesc: Derived from the URL and StartTLS. In production, remote ldap:// requires StartTLS or use ldaps://.
ldap.urlDesc: Prefer ldaps:// in production. Plain ldap:// without StartTLS is acceptable only to localhost in development.
ldap.startTlsDesc: Enable with ldap:// to negotiate TLS on the LDAP port (389). Not needed if you already use ldaps://.
ldap.tlsVerifyDesc: Disable only in lab: equivalent to trusting any certificate (MITM risk).
ldap.bindDnDesc: Service account with read rights on the directory to search for the user.
ldap.bindPasswordDesc: Write-only; leave empty to keep the password already stored on the server.
ldap.bindPwStateDesc: Shows whether a password is already stored. The API never returns the value.
ldap.baseDnDesc: Root under which users are searched (subtree scope).
ldap.userFilterDesc: Use the {usernameMark} placeholder for the sign-in identifier. If the filter does not contain {usernameMark}, the login attribute below completes the filter.
ldap.usernameAttrDesc: LDAP attribute name (e.g. sAMAccountName) used when the filter lacks {usernameMark}.
ldap.displayNameAttrDesc: Value copied to the ESOS display name when provisioning.
ldap.groupAttrDesc: Often memberOf in Active Directory; used for LDAP role mapping.
ldap.timeoutDesc: Connection and operation timeout on the LDAP client.
ldap.searchLimitDesc: User search is limited to {limit} entries on the server (not configurable).
ldap.customCaDesc: Not supported in this version: TLS trust follows the OS / Node trust store.
ldap.testDesc: Tests service account bind and a sample search (no end-user password). You can enter a bind password above for this test without saving configuration.

mapping.cardSubtitle: JIT, default role, and JSON rules. Without a matching rule, new JIT accounts get the default role below; existing accounts are not blocked.
mapping.jitEnableLabel: Create account on first external sign-in (JIT)
mapping.jitEnableHelp: If disabled, only existing or linked accounts can sign in via LDAP/OIDC.
mapping.jitDefaultRoleLabel: Default role for new JIT accounts
mapping.jitDefaultRoleDesc: Applied when no mapping rule grants a higher role for a new account. Existing accounts are not blocked by missing rules.
mapping.jitActiveDesc: If enabled, accounts created automatically on first OIDC/LDAP sign-in are immediately usable (per server rules).
mapping.oidcMaxRoleDesc: Upper bound for the role from OIDC rules (after mapping).
mapping.ldapMaxRoleDesc: Upper bound for the role from LDAP groups (after mapping).
mapping.rulesJsonDesc: Array of objects with match and role fields. OIDC rules use type oidc_claim; LDAP uses ldap_group_dn.

save.cardSubtitle: Applies settings on the server (client-side JSON validation before send). OIDC/LDAP tests do not save configuration.
save.actionsIntro: Save sends configuration to the server. The tests below do not change stored settings.
save.quickTestsIntro: Re-run tests after changing issuer, client_id, LDAP URL, or bind credentials.
save.noOidcTest: No OIDC test run since page load.
save.noLdapTest: No LDAP test run since page load.
save.ldapSuccessSample: Success — {count} entries in the search sample.
